summary.whatChanges: Reworks Zod's internal `toZod` type-level normalization: instead of rebuilding enum-like leaves through a mapped type, every non-object leaf is unioned with a private unique symbol. This makes the assignability check stricter, so plain literal unions no longer satisfy a numeric enum target. A test asserting the new rejection is added.
behaviorChanges: z.toZod<{ rank: NumericEnum }>() now rejects a schema built from z.union([z.literal(1), z.literal(2)]), which previously type-checked
All non-object leaf types, not just enum leaves, go through the normalization step during toZod comparison
z.enum(SomeEnum) against a matching enum target still passes, as before
risks: Existing TypeScript code using z.toZod with literal unions against enum targets will start failing compilation
Broadening normalization from enum leaves to all leaves may change matching for other primitive/branded/any cases beyond the single tested scenario
Relying on a unique symbol union to defeat structural identity is subtle and could interact unexpectedly with unions containing never or any
